title: Silas and the Spire
premise: Lena Delacroix, last of the oath-bound swordspeakers, keeps ledgers for a guild that trades in impossible things. When a blind date named Silas arrives at her door on the exact night a century-old book of prophecies names him, he is dragged into her world: his soul was sold before his birth to the court beneath the mountain, and the Spire that anchors it will claim him at winter's end. To save him, Lena must break her oath and steal back what the guild itself brokered — betraying the found family that raised her. In the end she pays the price of survival by surrendering her swordspeech to buy Silas's soul free, and they rebuild their family from the wreckage of both their old ones.
about_author: O. M. Eriksen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing trade ledgers in a northern port city before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about paperwork, oaths, and the people who fall through the cracks of both.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She closes the guild's books for the night, cataloguing traded miracles and debts, then remembers a blind date arranged by her foster sister Marta. The beat: loneliness beneath competence, a woman fluent in every currency but affection.

chapters.title: A Man Named in Advance
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. He arrives for dinner, charming and unmoored, a cartographer with no fixed address. Mid-meal, Lena's prophecy ledger opens itself to an entry dated tonight bearing his name. The beat: uncanny recognition — two strangers realizing they've met before the meeting.

chapters.title: What the Book Owes
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She reads the century-old entry: Silas's soul, sold pre-birth to the court beneath the mountain, collectible when the Spire aligns at winter's end. Guild law forbids disclosure to clients. She tells him anyway. The beat: first crack in her oath.

chapters.title: The Guildhouse Wakes
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The guildhouse responds to the breach — doors rearranging, senior partner Vess Corvane summoning them. Silas sees the guild's wonders and its menace in one night. The beat: wonder curdling into captivity; he is now inventory, not guest.

chapters.title: Terms of Custody
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Flashback-framed negotiation: the guild bought Silas's soul-debt cheap generations ago as an investment. Vess offers Silas protection in exchange for compliance. Lena watches her mentor lie beautifully. The beat: love against duty takes its first side.

chapters.title: Marta's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Lena's foster sister, a hedge-witch cook, feeds them and tells the truth about the guild: it raised orphans like Lena by owning them. Marta urges escape. The beat: found family asserting itself against institutional family.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Map
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. He maps the guildhouse from memory — habit, not plan — and discovers a sealed stair descending toward the mountain road. Lena catches him; instead of reporting it, she helps. The beat: complicity as intimacy.

chapters.title: Swordspeech
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She reveals her oath-gift: words spoken through steel become binding law. One true sentence per year, already spent keeping the guild's ledgers honest. She has nothing left until spring. The beat: the price of survival made concrete — power rationed by time.

chapters.title: Flight Across the Salt Flats
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They flee by night toward the mountain, pursued by guild retrievers. A storm forces closeness; Silas admits he's always felt borrowed, provisional. The beat: two rootless people choosing each other mid-crisis.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Toll
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A river-ferry spirit demands payment in memory. Silas offers freely; Lena stops him and pays with a memory of Vess instead, protecting him and losing part of her past. The beat: sacrifice performed quietly, without witness.

chapters.title: Village of the Sold
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. They reach a village of others whose souls were sold at birth — hollow-eyed, long-lived, waiting. An elder recognizes Silas's name in the village registry. The beat: horror of scale; he is one entry in a vast ledger.

chapters.title: The Elder's Bargain
chapters.summary: Elder Sef's POV. She explains the court beneath the mountain honors only theft: souls must be stolen back, not repurchased. But theft requires a speaker's word to open the court's doors. The beat: hope with a hook — rescue requires Lena's last oath-word.

chapters.title: Retrieval
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Guild retrievers corner them; Marta, having followed, turns her kitchen-magic against them and buys an escape at the cost of her own capture. The beat: found family paying installments on each other's freedom.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Grief-driven, they enter the mountain's throat — a market of bottled voices, a river of unspent years. Silas begins to fade as the Spire's alignment nears. The beat: dread deepening into tenderness under deadline.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. They stand before the Undercourt: a chandelier of contracts, a monarch who is the guild's original founder. The founder offers Silas his soul if Lena signs over the guild's ledgers — all its impossible debts. The beat: temptation shaped exactly like mercy.

chapters.title: Winter's End Alignment
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The Spire aligns; his collection begins. He experiences himself being read aloud, page by page. Lena refuses the founder's bargain because accepting would enslave every soul in the ledgers. The beat: love refusing a poisoned rescue.

chapters.title: The Theft
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Following Sef's law, she commits the theft: speaking her final oath-word through her sword, she declares Silas's soul stolen property and herself the thief, binding the court's own contract-law against it. The beat: climax — her gift spent, her voice gone to steel forever.

chapters.title: Collapse of the Chandelier
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The court unravels as its contracts contradict themselves; the founder shatters into archived paper. They run as the mountain exhales a century of freed souls. The beat: catharsis — the ledger burning upward like reversed snowfall.

chapters.title: What Was Bought Back
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Above ground, whole again but changed, Silas finds Lena voiceless, her swordspeech gone. He speaks for both of them now, telling her what she cannot say. The beat: grief braided with gratitude; roles reversed.

chapters.title: Reckoning with Vess
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. They return to free Marta and confront Vess, whose empire of debts is collapsing. Vess, defeated, admits she kept Lena close out of something like love. Lena chooses exile over succession. The beat: duty released, not fulfilled.

chapters.title: The New Ledger
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. The three of them reopen the guildhouse as something smaller and kinder: a shop that returns impossible things rather than trading them. First customer: Elder Sef, come to reclaim her own sold name. The beat: found family formalized as vocation.

chapters.title: Silas and the Spire
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, closing. Spring. He maps the rebuilt town while Lena writes her first unsanctioned sentence in a private journal — ordinary words, hers alone. The Spire stands empty on the horizon. The beat: quiet resolution; survival's price paid, and worth it.
